title: 2026 West Maui Taxpayers Association Candidate Forum

recap.headline: West Maui Taxpayers Association forum: State House 14, Maui mayor and three council races
recap.in_60_seconds: The West Maui Taxpayers Association held a forum for primary election candidates. Each candidate gave a timed statement of three minutes, or four minutes for the Upcountry and Kahului council candidates, with no live question-and-answer period. Audience members wrote questions on a whiteboard for candidates to photograph and answer later. Twenty candidates took part: five for State House District 14, seven for Maui County mayor, and two, two and four for the Upcountry, Kahului and Wailuku-Waiheʻe-Waikapū council seats. Statements covered Lahaina recovery, housing, affordability, water, short-term rentals and Bill 9, public safety and campaign money.

event.name: 2026 West Maui Taxpayers Association Candidate Forum

recap.moderated_by: a West Maui Taxpayers Association host

answers.summary: Said she founded Save Honolulu Coalition, was on the county council eight years, ran for mayor, and is going up for a third House term. Said she switched from Democrat to Republican about a month ago, citing waste, fraud, and abuse and being disrespected. Said she made connections in DC and can be a vessel for voters at the federal level.

Said being raised in Lahina with roots in Mala village, a founding member of Lahina Strong, vice president of Safe Honolulua Coalition and a board of water supply member. Described Ola as our communities come first, living in balance with Aina and accountability in government. Cited a regenerative tourism model and the Lahina Energy Partnership with the National Laboratories of the Rockies.

Said he is a proud Luna graduate, US Army veteran, father and coach who runs a community distribution hub serving over a thousand people and feeding over 400 a week. Said that if elected, his team, with people who know infrastructure and affordable housing, education, and fire prevention, is ready to go to work day one.

Said she is a career educator and that anyone who attended Lahinol Luna High School over the last 30 odd years probably knows her. Proposed raising income eligibility limits to ease the general excise tax burden on lower income families, partnering with Habitat for Humanity on workforce housing, and expanding broadband. Said she is running as a Democrat to make changes from within.

Said he is a husband, father of three and West Maui resident involved in Lahina's recovery through business, nonprofit work, county boards and community advocacy. Listed priorities: a recovery plan showing where funding is going, which agencies are responsible and timelines; affordability and opportunity. Said he would use relationships to push for West Maui from day one.

Said he is running for reelection as mayor with 38 years protecting the community as a prosecuting attorney, judge and mayor. Said over 500 homes have been built, 700 permits approved, 40 days is the time to apply for a permit, boating operations at Lahina Harbor restored, and fire prevention staffing increased. Said water is increasing from 45% to 93% community and publicly determined.

Said he arrived in Hawaiʻi in 1957, is a Vietnam veteran who served 20 years in SEAL Team One, and lives in Haʻikū. Said he will not make promises but will examine the issues and follow through methodically with a new plan, working with the council and community. Said he will ensure candidates get copies of the whiteboard questions and respond.

Said he is 41, from the Midwest, with no wife or kids, and volunteers in the community daily after his desk job. Supports more transparency and accountability, including live-streamed budget review and online public input. Promised to give 45% to 55% of his paycheck to community organizations and families, and urged higher turnout, saying 50,000 of 113,000 voters voted in the last general.

Said affordability is her main pillar, including rolling back costs, fees and taxes and affordable homes. Proposed using taxes from Bill Nine homes for up to $80,000 in down payment assistance for first-time home buyers, plus a $500 rental gap for up to three years. Said she will take the 2018 fire mitigation plans and the flood mitigation plan so Kīhei does not flood again and Up Country gets meters.

Said he first came to Nāpili in 1985 and worked at NASA, Sandia and SETI focused on wastewater. Proposed savings officers in each department, county rebates for those netting under six figures, zero property tax on kuleana lands with managed watersheds, higher taxes on ultra-high-net-worth holdings, and free buses. Said he is running to get wastewater disinfection on Maui's north and south shores.

Said residents told him corruption in government is their top concern, and said front-runners Denise, Yuki and Richard got caught up in it. Said he lives on Social Security only and takes no fundraising, gifts or paid advertising, and that a mayor should take no more than 25% of the current salary. Questioned why the $1.5 billion county budget keeps rising.

Said she was born and raised on Maui, her family has been here five generations, and she evacuated her home in Kula. Supports rent stabilization rather than a harsh cap, interim housing for the homeless, and more agricultural parks, noting Maui has one while ʻAʻahu and the Big Island have four each. Proposed taxing non-resident vacation homes worth over five million.

Said he is a ko farmer, father, grandfather and great-grandfather who has lived on Maui for 45 years. Said he is running to listen to the community and find solutions, and that people cannot afford to eat native crops. Said that when the Corona virus first hit, he was a bridge between farmers who lost their market and those impacted.

Said he is married, a father of four, and used to own Dickinson Square in Lahina, which burned down with the fire. Said he would first try to find water, whether drilling or building reservoirs, then affordable housing and sustainable development. Said Bill Nine isn't over and isn't fair to people who followed the rules.

Said he has no political experience but 27-plus years in information technology. Supports improving public safety and housing, saying mainland companies buying housing drive up rents. Supports limiting but not eliminating short-term rentals and taxing them more, and said he needs to research Bill 9 further.

Said she is a retired 22-year US Navy and Naval Reserve veteran and single mother of seven who refuses corporate campaign money. Supports modern emergency infrastructure, fire adapted landscapes, a transparent recovery process, the restoration and revitalization of Lahina, and resident first generational housing. Promised to listen and ensure tax dollars are managed responsibly.

Said he has been an attorney for about 25 years, including three years with the Maui County Council, and has worked in environmental law, farming and water rights. Said he signed the Our Hawaiʻi pledge not to take corporate or developer money and asked other candidates to sign it.

Said he is 49 and a certified arborist and general foreman managing over 30 employees in line clearance, hazardous tree removal and wildfire mitigation. Said he is a pastor who ministers weekly to people in recovery and in prisons and helps the unsheltered. Said he wants to bring that servant heart to leadership.

Said she has served 10 years on county boards, including the Maui Redevelopment Agency and as vice chair of the Maui Planning Commission, where she voted no on Bill 9. Said local people are leaving for lack of jobs and housing. Said she has been a property manager for over 20 years and has run over 10 small businesses.

Said he took the pledge to not take corporate or PAC contributions and has worked as an organizer for the Hawaiʻi Worker Center, including with Lahina Crossroads tenants when the county bought the building. Listed four pillars: affordable housing, low cost or free preschool, services at community centers, and reduced grocery costs using the commissary model.
